* Driven and motivated and eager to learn

Creativ Digital is looking for a capable experienced freelance developer to help support and improve modern web, mobile and AI\-enabled client products.

* Flexible part\-time hours — typically 15–25 hours per week initially

* Reviewing and taking over existing web and mobile applications

* Building new product features across frontend, backend and mobile

* Working with AI features, LLM APIs and agent\-assisted development workflows
* Communicating clearly with product owners and Creativ’s delivery team

* 5\+ years’ commercial software\-development experience
* Strong React and modern JavaScript/TypeScript skills
* Experience with React Native and Expo for mobile app development
* Solid Node.js, APIs and PostgreSQL/database experience
* Experience supporting live cloud applications — AWS, Supabase, Cloudflare or similar

* A practical, reliable approach to debugging, QA and safe releases
* Ability to work independently and explain technical issues in plain English

Nice to have

* Agency, consulting, freelance or fractional technical\-lead experience
* GitHub Actions, CI/CD, Stripe, Twilio, Sentry or similar tools
* Experience with SaaS, subscription products, customer portals or mobile apps

Engagement details

* Sydney\-based preferred
* Freelance contractor or part\-time arrangement
* Remote\-first, flexible schedule
* Immediate start available
* Please include your hourly rate, availability and links to relevant work

* **Full\-time continuing role (HEW Level 10, Band 1\)**
* **Macquarie University, Wallumattagal Campus, North Ryde**

 ***A rare breadth of WHS: research, health, science and higher education on a single campus***

  

Macquarie University is looking for an experienced work health and safety professional to lead our central WHS function. As **Head of Workplace Health and Safety**, you will guide the framework, systems and team that keep more than 10,000 staff, students, contractors and visitors physically and psychologically safe across a busy campus that includes research laboratories, teaching spaces, hospital and health facilities, commercial entities and outdoor operations.

  

This is a genuinely broad portfolio. You will set the WHS strategy for the University and its Controlled Entities, oversee injury management and workers compensation, act as the trusted adviser to senior leaders on complex safety matters, and translate WHS performance data into clear reporting for University Council, committees and boards. It is a role where governance rigour and practical, people\-centred judgement matter in equal measure.

  

Reporting to the Chief Risk Officer and working within the Group Risk portfolio, you will join a team that is trusted, well supported and closely connected to executive decision\-making. If you enjoy improving systems, developing capable teams and seeing the real\-world results of a mature safety culture, this is an opportunity to make a visible contribution at scale.

 **About the Role**

  

Working as part of the Group Risk portfolio within the Office of the Vice\-President, Finance and Resources, you will oversee the University's WHS Program, Injury Management and Return to Work Program, and workers compensation insurance and claims management.

  

Your responsibilities will include:

  

* Setting and delivering the Group WHS strategy across the University and its Controlled Entities, strengthening safety culture and enabling continuous improvement.
* Ensuring due diligence and compliance with the NSW WHS Act, Regulations and Codes of Practice.
* Guiding and developing a team of eight WHS, injury management, emergency management and hazardous materials specialists.
* Owning the University's WHS framework (policies, procedures, training, systems, reporting and performance management) to protect physical and psychological health and safety.
* Delivering complex, cross\-functional WHS programs and projects, managing scope, risk and stakeholder alignment.
* Managing the WHS operating budget.
* Advising senior leaders on WHS and rehabilitation matters, balancing better\-practice approaches with statutory obligations and operational realities.
* Overseeing injury management, workers compensation, return to work and early intervention, including external provider relationships, to improve outcomes and reduce harm and cost.
* Overseeing WHS consultation and governance and translating WHS analytics into clear reporting for University Council, committees and boards.
* Managing regulator engagement and reporting (for example SafeWork NSW), and required registrations and permits with CASA, the ATO and the Commonwealth Department of Health, Disability and Ageing.

An exciting opportunity for a Teaching \& Leadership or Teaching \& Research academic to develop and contribute to innovative and impactful teaching in the Doctor of Physiotherapy and other Health Sciences courses.

* Appointment Type: Full\-time, 2\-year fixed term appointment
* Located at Macquarie University (Wallumattagal Campus, North Ryde)

**The Role**


Macquarie University is proud to offer a highly respected, innovative and evidenced\-based Doctor of Physiotherapy (DPT) post graduate degree and is seeking a **Lecturer or Senior Lecturer** to join our dedicated and ambitious Physiotherapy team. Our course combines contemporary coursework with over 1,000 hours of supervised clinical placements, providing students with an excellent grounding for their future career.  



  

Reporting to the Head of School, Health Sciences and Nursing, and Course Director of Physiotherapy, you will utilise your professional and industry experience to make a critical contribution to the development and delivery of teaching within the DPT program and other Health Sciences courses. We seek a highly motivated and collaborative physiotherapist to join our School for appointment to either the Teaching and Leadership or Teaching and Research job family. You will have expertise in teaching and convening Physiotherapy and Health Sciences related programs, and research in these areas.

  

The Macquarie University Academic Job Family Framework recognises and rewards the breadth of academic work.

  

The Teaching \& Leadership Academic is a specialist teaching and leadership role for academic staff who demonstrate excellence in teaching and leadership. As a specialist role, Teaching \& Leadership Academic staff dedicate their workload contribution to Teaching, Teaching Leadership, and Service. Graduate research degree supervision may also form a part of teaching\-related activities in this job family.

  

The Teaching \& Research Academic dedicates their workload contribution to teaching, research and service including graduate research student supervision within their research as well as fulfilling service roles to the School and/or Faculty.

 **About Us**


The Faculty of Medicine, Health and Human Sciences (FMHHS) is ambitiously pushing the boundaries of progressive thinking and challenging what’s possible to solve some of the big issues of our time, both nationally and on a global scale.

  

The faculty’s current education suite includes courses in clinical science, physiotherapy, medicine and public health, psychology, cognitive sciences, linguistics, audiology, and speech pathology. The Faculty forms part of Macquarie University Health, an integrated academic health sciences enterprise which incorporates Macquarie University Hospital and primary and speciality clinics. Macquarie University is seeking an outstanding academic to join the **School of Computing** in the Faculty of Science and Engineering.

  

This is an **open\-rank appointment**, with the successful candidate appointed at **Lecturer (Level B), Senior Lecturer (Level C), or Associate Professor (Level D)** depending on their qualifications, experience, academic achievements and leadership profile.

  

We welcome applications from talented academics working across **any major area of Computer Science**. Areas of particular interest include, but are not limited to:

  

* Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
* Generative AI, Foundation Models and Large Language Models
* Data Science and Data Analytics
* Data Management and Information Retrieval
* Cybersecurity, Privacy and Trust
* Software Engineering and Programming Languages
* Computer Systems and Architecture
* Cloud, Edge and Distributed Computing
* Computer Networks and Internet Technologies
* Human\-Computer Interaction and Human\-Centred Computing
* Computer Vision and Multimedia
* Natural Language Processing
* Robotics and Autonomous Systems
* Algorithms, Optimisation and Theoretical Computer Science
* Responsible, Trustworthy and Secure Computing
* Computational Science and interdisciplinary applications of computing
* Emerging areas of Computer Science

  

We are particularly interested in candidates undertaking **ambitious, high\-quality and impactful research**, with the potential to strengthen and expand the School's research capabilities and contribute to its national and international profile.

  

The successful candidate will contribute to research, teaching and academic service appropriate to their level of appointment. This may include developing, teaching and convening undergraduate and postgraduate units, supervising Higher Degree Research students, building research collaborations, attracting external research funding, engaging with industry and government, and contributing to academic leadership within the School, Faculty and University.

  

We encourage applications from candidates with both established and emerging research profiles, including talented early\-career academics demonstrating an exceptional trajectory.

 **About Us**

  

You will be joining a growing **School of Computing** in the Faculty of Science and Engineering with a fast\-rising international reputation.

  

The School is home to more than 60 academic staff, over 150 research students, and close to 3,500 undergraduate and postgraduate coursework students. It offers a broad range of contemporary undergraduate and postgraduate programs and has a strong and growing research culture.

  

The School provides a collaborative environment in which academics are encouraged to pursue ambitious research agendas, develop interdisciplinary and industry partnerships, contribute to innovative teaching, and build internationally recognised academic careers.

  

This appointment represents an opportunity for an outstanding academic to contribute to the next phase of growth and development of Computer Science at Macquarie University.

 **About You – Selection Criteria**

  

The successful candidate will be an ambitious and collegial academic with a strong commitment to research and education. We are looking for candidates who can demonstrate achievement and potential **relative to their career stage and the academic level for which they are being considered**.

 **Selection Criteria – All Applicants (Levels B, C and D)**

  

Applicants at all levels should demonstrate:

  

* A PhD in Computer Science, Computing, or a closely related discipline.
* A strong and coherent research program in one or more areas of contemporary Computer Science.
* A high\-quality research publication record, relative to career stage and opportunity, demonstrated through publications in respected international journals, conferences or other recognised scholarly venues appropriate to the candidate's field.
* Evidence of the quality, originality, significance or potential impact of their research.
* Demonstrated capability and commitment to delivering high\-quality and innovative teaching at undergraduate and/or postgraduate levels.
* Capacity to contribute to curriculum development and teaching in areas relevant to the School's undergraduate and postgraduate programs.
* Evidence of the ability to supervise, or the potential to successfully supervise, Higher Degree Research students.
* Evidence of the ability to develop research collaborations within academia and/or with industry, government or other external partners.
* Evidence of success, or clear potential for success, in attracting external research funding appropriate to career stage.
* High\-level oral and written communication skills, with demonstrated ability to work effectively and collegially with students, academic and professional staff, collaborators and external stakeholders.
* A demonstrated commitment to contributing positively to an inclusive, collaborative and high\-performing academic environment.

  

Industry engagement, interdisciplinary research, international collaboration, entrepreneurship, translation or demonstrated research impact beyond academia will be highly regarded.

 **Additional Selection Criteria – Senior Lecturer (Level C)**

  

Candidates seeking appointment at **Senior Lecturer (Level C)** should, in addition to the criteria above, demonstrate:

  

* An established and internationally recognised research profile, with a sustained record of high\-quality research outputs and evidence of increasing research influence and impact.
* A demonstrated record of successful supervision of Higher Degree Research students, including contribution to the development of research students and early\-career researchers.
* A demonstrated record of attracting external research funding, or substantial evidence of the capacity to lead competitive research funding applications and funded research projects.
* Evidence of leadership in research, teaching, curriculum development, academic programs, research groups, professional activities, or other areas relevant to the School.
* A demonstrated capacity to develop and lead productive research collaborations and contribute to building research capability within a School or broader academic environment.
* Evidence of a growing national and international reputation in the candidate's field.

 **Additional Selection Criteria – Associate Professor (Level D)**

  

Candidates seeking appointment at **Associate Professor (Level D)** should, in addition to the criteria above, demonstrate:

  

* A distinguished and internationally recognised research profile, with a sustained record of outstanding scholarly achievement, research influence and impact.
* A substantial record of research leadership, including leadership of significant research programs, teams, centres, networks or major collaborative initiatives.
* A strong record of attracting and leading significant external research funding from competitive, government, industry or other sources.
* A strong record of successful Higher Degree Research supervision and research mentorship, including demonstrated contribution to developing research students, early\-career academics and research capability.
* Significant academic leadership in areas such as research strategy, education, curriculum, academic programs, organisational development, external engagement or professional leadership.
* Demonstrated ability to build strategic collaborations with leading national and international researchers, industry, government and/or other external partners.
* Evidence of a strong national and international standing in the candidate's discipline and the capacity to enhance the research reputation, visibility and impact of the School of Computing and Macquarie University.
* Demonstrated capacity to provide intellectual and academic leadership and to contribute strategically to the future development of the School.

 **How to Apply**

* your curriculum vitae;
* a cover letter outlining your interest in the position and the academic level for which you wish to be considered; and
* a statement addressing how your experience and achievements align with the relevant selection criteria.

 **Please note that applications for this position are only being accepted from Australian citizens, permanent residents, and those currently residing in Australia with full working rights.**
